newsitem.title: JAPAN: Better Japan output helps quell fears on economy.
newsitem.headline: Better Japan output helps quell fears on economy.

text.p: Japan's industrial output for July was higher than expected and while the rise was not enough to point to greater economic strength, it helped quell fears that the nation's recovery might be taking a turn for the worse.

According to government data released on Friday, industrial production rose a preliminary 4.1 percent month on month -- much higher than economists' predictions which averaged an increase of 3.4 percent.

"Today's figure is a very strong figure, but the total situation is not so strong. Recently, production in the mining and manufacturing sectors is still a case of one step forward and one step back," said Masaru Takagi, chief economist at Fuji Research Institute.
Economists said the July figure was still essentially a rebound after a sharp fall in June. But they said a one percent downturn month on month in inventories was still a good sign.

They added that a forecast by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) of a 1.1 percent rise in industrial output for the July to September quarter was enough to stave off fears that the economy's recovery might falter.

The closely watched industrial output figure -- considered a key barometer of future economic health -- was the focus of even more attention than usual after other data earlier this week showed business sentiment taking a surprise downturn.

In the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly corporate survey, or "tankan", released on Wednesday, the key diffusion index of major manufacturers for August fell to minus seven from May's minus three. Most analysts had expected a modest rise.

The diffusion index measures the percentage of firms which expect their business environment to improve, minus the percentage that expect it to worsen. The higher the figure, the better the economic outlook.
The weak number prompted BOJ officials and politicians alike to declare that while the economy was maintaining a gradual comeback, the path of sustained recovery may not be smooth.
MITI officials agreed that the industrial output data was in line with this assessment.

"For those expecting the pace of economic recovery to accelerate with time, the current pace of recovery may seem a little weak. We share the view of the Bank of Japan that the economic recovery may not necessarily be without setbacks," one official said.
